subject: Banking
title: The Conflict of Interest Problem
description: Learn The Conflict of Interest Problem in one minute.

hook.text: Investment banks research, rate, and sell stocks to clients. They also earn fees from the companies they rate.

buildup.text: Before 2003, analysts routinely gave buy ratings to companies that paid the bank advisory fees. Honesty hurt revenue.

discovery.text: Eliot Spitzer's investigations revealed that analysts privately called stocks 'garbage' while publicly recommending.

twist.text: Regulations now require separating research from banking.

climax.text: Investment banking's core conflict is serving two masters. Honest advice sometimes means losing a fee-paying client.

punchline.text: Rate it 'buy' publicly, call it 'garbage' privately. Conflicts persist.

quiz.question: What did Spitzer's investigations reveal about analyst ratings?
options: Analysts publicly rated stocks 'buy' while privately calling them garbage
